newsitem.title: USA: FBI probes corruption in El Paso city government.
newsitem.headline: FBI probes corruption in El Paso city government.

text.p: FBI agents have been brought in to investigate corruption allegations involving city employees and contractors in the southwest Texas border city of El Paso, officials said Thursday.
Mayor Larry Francis said the probe was focusing on the city's engineering department and bidding processes for multimillion-dollar construction projects over the past seven years.
Francis told a news conference that several area contractors are also under close scrutiny, and that arrests are expected in the next few months.
He did not detail the alleged crimes, but said the Federal Bureau of Investigation was helping the Internal Revenue Service and the local U.S. Attorney's office.
"All I can say is this is an extensive investigation involving volumes of evidence," Francis said, adding that the investigation might spread to other departments of the city government.
Police Chief Russ Leach said the alleged corruption involving city employees and outside contractors had led to sub-standard construction on some projects.
"This is extremely serious and we are committed to seeking charges against those who may have committed the crimes," Leach said.
